children.description: Calls a delegated helper made, nested under the call that started it, so a reopened conversation redraws the delegation rather than collapsing it into one result.

content.description: What it produced: text, a change to a file, or a picture.

oldText.description: What was there. Absent for a new file, or where the previous contents are not known.

path.description: Which file, as a workspace path.

truncated.description: One of the two sides was too large to send whole.

path.description: Where it is, as a workspace path. A path rather than the bytes, because the workspace already serves it, sending it inline would bloat every stored record, and this way the picture stays openable afterwards.

status.description: How it went.

target.description: What it acted on, in one line: a file, a command, an address.

thinking.description: What the agent was reasoning about around this call.

messages.description: The conversation, in order. Each block of the agent's prose is its own message with the tools that block introduced, which is what reproduces the way it actually unfolded.

attachments.description: Files attached to this message, as workspace paths.

checkpointId.description: The saved point this message can be rewound to. Looked up on each read rather than stored, so what is offered is exactly what is still there to go back to.

notes.description: What the sandbox added to this message before the model saw it. Carried on the message rather than as rows of their own, because they genuinely were part of what was sent.

text.description: The note itself, which is also exactly what the model was told.

title.description: The one line a reader sees, on a row that opens to the text below.

noticeAction.description: A one-press follow-up this recorded notice offers, by name. The chat decides what it does and whether it still applies.

placed.description: A person wrote this in the agent's voice, with no turn behind it. Marked for the human re-reading the conversation months later, so their own words do not pass as the agent's. The agent itself never sees the mark.

role.description: Who said it. A notice is neither side: it is something that happened to the turn, recorded so a reopened conversation can say it. Without those, a turn a provider refused ends on the user's message and reads as broken.

sentAt.description: When it was sent, in milliseconds. On the user's rows only, because that is the only moment actually known: a turn's own frames arrive with no clock, so stamping the agent's rows could only ever mean the whole turn's start or end.

thinking.description: What the agent was reasoning about.

tools.description: The tool calls this part of the turn made.

sessionId.description: The provider session behind the last turn, when there is one.

account.description: Which of that provider's connected accounts pays for the turn. Leave it out for the first one.

actsAs.description: Which persona the turn speaks as out in the world. Not the same as which account pays for it.

agent.description: Which model provider serves this turn. Leave it out for Claude.

allowedTools.description: Narrow the turn to these tools. Leave it out for everything the runtime has. For a turn driven by an outside message this list is the real boundary, because prompt wording is only advice.

attachments.description: Files to hand the agent along with the prompt, as workspace paths. Upload them first.

autoLand.description: Whether this turn's work merges into the workspace when it finishes. Overrides the conversation's own setting for this turn only.

editorContext.description: What the user has open in their editor, folded into the prompt so that pointing words like "this" resolve.

endLine.description: Last line of the selection, counting from one.

file.description: The file open in the editor, as a workspace path.

selection.description: The selected text itself. Cut it down before sending if it is long: this is context, not an upload.

startLine.description: First line of the selection, counting from one. Leave both out when the whole file is the context.

effort.description: How hard the model should think, where the provider offers a choice.

fast.description: Ask for the same work at a higher rate for a higher price. A request rather than a promise: the answer says what actually happened.

forkOf.description: Where this conversation was cut from, on its first turn only. Only the client knows this, so only the client can say it.

conversationId.description: The conversation this one was cut from.

files.description: Which files the fork opens on: "now" is the workspace as it stands, "then" is the files as they were at the cut, which needs a private copy.

keep.description: How many of that conversation's messages to copy in before this turn runs.

harness.description: Which agentic loop runs the turn. Leave it out to use each provider's own.

isolated.description: Work in this conversation's own private copy of the repos rather than the shared tree, so several agents can work at once. Needs a conversation id.

model.description: Which model to use. Leave it out for the provider's default.

origin.description: Set by the sandbox alone: this turn opened a conversation on behalf of a message from outside rather than a person.

outsideWake.description: Content from outside caused this turn, and what to call the source. It is what makes the sandbox treat the turn as carrying somebody else's words.

permissionMode.description: How tool calls are gated: ask each time, accept file edits, propose a plan first, or run everything. The agent can move itself between these mid-turn.

prompt.description: What to say to the agent. May be empty if you are only attaching files.

sessionId.description: Resume this provider session instead of starting a fresh one.

thinking.description: Whether to show the model's reasoning as it works.

tierHold.description: Run exactly the model that was picked, even when the turn looks simple enough for a cheaper one. The judgement is still recorded; nothing is substituted.

title.description: A title for a conversation this turn is opening. Ignored for a conversation that already has one.

unattended.description: Nobody chose a model for this turn because a screen started it rather than a person. The sandbox then fills in the model its owner picked for unwatched work.

worktreeBase.description: Pin a new private copy to these exact commits instead of today's workspace. Used when several agents must start from identical files.

failed.description: The conversations this press could not put away, each with the reason, so the board can say it instead of reporting silence.

id.description: Which conversation stayed on the board.

reason.description: Why its working copy could not be released, in the words the failure came with.

activity.description: What it is doing at this moment.

target.description: What it reached for that tool with: a file, a command, a URL.

todo.description: The item on its own list that it is working through.

tool.description: The last tool it reached for.

costUsd.description: What it has cost so far, in dollars. A helper agent's spend is its own and is not folded in here.

diff.description: Everything it has written, measured from where it started. Independent of how much has been merged.

deletions.description: Lines removed.

effort.description: How hard that turn was told to think.

failure.description: Why the last turn failed, in the words it died on. Absent unless it did, and cleared the moment it runs again. Carried here because the word error on its own is not an answer, least of all for a run nobody was watching.

fast.description: Whether that turn asked for higher speed. What was asked for, not what was served.

forkedFrom.description: The conversation this one was cut from. Recorded once and never cleared: it is the relationship, not a pending state.

harness.description: Which agentic loop it runs on.

id.description: The conversation id, which is how every other call addresses it.

landRequested.description: A collaborator has asked a maintainer to merge this work. Cleared by whichever merge or discard answers it. Absent means nobody is waiting.

landedMessage.description: What this conversation's merged work is called, once the drafting above has finished. It arrives on the same push that ends the draft, so the promise and the answer travel together.

breaking.description: What this change takes away, for anything already relying on it. Nearly always absent: it is for removals, not for additions.

note.description: The same change said to somebody who uses the product, for a repository that keeps a changelog. Usually absent, because most changes are not ones a user would notice.

subject.description: One line saying what the merged work did, read off the code rather than off the opening request. A conversation that asks for an audit and then spends four turns fixing what it found needs a subject about the fixes.

landedMessageDraft.description: The whole story of this merge's commit message being written: which models were asked, how long each took, what refused and in what words. Forgotten on restart, which is right, because a restart also killed the drafting it describes.

outcome.description: How it ended. Absent means it is still going.

reason.description: The one-line account of a failure, for a screen with one line to spend. The steps carry each model's own words.

startedAt.description: When the drafting began, in milliseconds.

steps.description: Each model that was asked, in the order they were spent, so the list is the timeline. Empty with no outcome means the diff is still being read.

at.description: When it started being asked, in milliseconds. Absent for one that was skipped, which cost no time.

ms.description: How long it took. Absent while it is still being asked.

reason.description: Why it refused, in its own words.

status.description: How this one went. Skipped means it was not asked at all, because it refused a few minutes ago and the walk stepped over it.

landedPresence.description: Present only when some of what it merged has since been thrown away. Absent is the steady state: its presence is the signal, so an ordinary card spends no line on it.

present.description: How many of them are still there, either pending or committed.

loop.description: The loop driving this conversation, if one is. Absent for an ordinary conversation, which is nearly all of them.

maxIterations.description: How many rounds it will attempt before giving up.

state.description: How the loop is going.

model.description: What its last turn ran with. Kept per conversation so opening it restores the choices made in it, rather than whatever some other tab last picked.

origin.description: Where the conversation came from when nobody typed it: a chat mention, a visitor's message, a webhook. Absent means a person started it.

provider.description: Which model provider it runs on.

seenAt.description: When somebody last opened it, in milliseconds. Newer activity than this is what makes it unread. Kept by the sandbox rather than by a browser, so clearing site data or picking up a phone does not resurrect every badge.

sessionId.description: The provider session behind the last turn. It is retired whenever the model or account changes.

startedAt.description: When the running turn started, in milliseconds. Absent when none is running.

status.description: What it is doing. Stopping and stopped are the two halves of somebody pressing stop, because a cancel is not instant; resuming means the sandbox is already putting right whatever killed the turn.

subagents.description: Helper agents this one delegated to. Absent means it never has, which is most conversations. Their spend is their own and is not folded into this conversation's cost.

total.description: Helpers it has started over its whole life.

thinking.description: Whether that turn showed its reasoning.

tier.description: How hard its last turn looked to the complexity judge. What the next turn's preview needs, not what actually ran.

tierHold.description: Whether this conversation is pinned to the picked model, so a turn that looks simple is never moved to a cheaper one.

title.description: What to call it: the first prompt cut to one line, unless somebody renamed it.

toolUses.description: Tools it has used, over its whole life.

updatedAt.description: When it last did something, in milliseconds. Reading it does not count.

watches.description: Outside conditions this conversation is parked on, each of which will wake it. Absent means none, which is nearly every conversation: an armed watch is why a finished-looking agent starts working by itself, and why a hosted machine will not go idle.

deadlineAt.description: When it gives up and wakes the conversation anyway, in milliseconds. Every watch has one.

id.description: The daemon's handle for this watch, the same one the agent was given when it armed it.

note.description: The agent's own line on what it is waiting for.

workflow.description: The workflow run this conversation is a step of. Without it, a four-step run reads as four unrelated conversations that happen to have started together.

index.description: This step's place in the workflow, counting from one.

runId.description: The run this belongs to, which is how a board groups its steps together.

step.description: Which step this conversation is on now. It moves when steps are chained.

total.description: How many steps the workflow has.

on.description: Which of your machines to put it on.

values.description: Its settings, including the address it should answer on.

template.description: Which kind of app to scaffold, by its key in the template list.

repo.description: Which repository.

app.description: The app's name, which is also its folder.

kind.description: What sort of app it is: the template it came from, or the framework worked out from its dependencies. Absent when it was found purely by having a dev script.

previewUrl.description: Where to open it. Absent when this sandbox has no outside address.

running.description: Whether its dev server is up.

description.description: What picking it means.

label.description: The choice, in a few words.

preview.description: Something to look at while deciding: a mock-up, a snippet, a layout.

options.description: The choices offered. A free-text answer is always possible as well.

prompt.description: What was said to start it, so a window that did not start the turn can still draw the message.

seq.description: How many frames already exist. Everything at or below this number is replay; everything above it is live.

startedAt.description: When it started, in milliseconds, so a window joining late can show how long it has been going.

clean.description: How many files would apply regardless, so a screen can say how much is being held back by how little and offer to take it. Zero alongside an empty list means the repository could not be reached at all.

mainBranch.description: The branch your own checkout is on, which is what the conversation has to rebase onto. Carried because only the sandbox can see it. Absent where there is no name to give.

paths.description: The files that genuinely would not apply. Not the whole change: reporting everything whenever the cause could not be pinned down turned four real conflicts into a wall of fourteen.

path.description: Which file.

reason.description: Why it would not merge, and the three have nothing in common but the symptom. Your own uncommitted edits on that path, where yours is the copy at risk. repo.description: Which repository.

text.description: The note itself, which is also exactly what the model was told.

title.description: The one line a reader sees, on a row that opens to the text below.

oldText.description: What was there. Absent for a new file, or where the previous contents are not known.

path.description: Which file, as a workspace path.

truncated.description: One of the two sides was too large to send whole.

content.description: The item, as the agent wrote it.

status.description: Where it is.

description.description: What it does.

hint.description: What its argument should look like, shown after the name.

name.description: What to type, without the leading slash.

contextWindow.description: How much the model can hold. The gap between these two is how close the conversation is to being compacted.

tokens.description: How much the latest request sent, all told.

displayName.description: A short phrase for the button, such as read file.

kind.description: The agent wants to use a tool it needs permission for.

path.description: Which file it concerns, when it concerns one.

reason.description: Why it is asking at all: a rule, the current mode, something that looked risky.

toolName.description: Which tool it wants to use.

credits.description: Your own meter, as the platform stated it.

allowance.description: How many credits the period gives.

description.description: What it does.

probation.description: The listing is new and has not yet served enough runs cleanly to be trusted. The honest form of listed automatically but not vouched for, and the person approving the spend is who should know it.

request.description: Exactly what would be sent, so you can see what leaves before agreeing to it.

why.description: The agent's case for spending, and the only words on this card that are the agent's.

event.description: Progress. Each one replaces the last: a label, not a log.

data.description: The answer itself, in whatever shape that service returns.

event.description: The answer. Exactly one of these ends a run.

card.description: Which connection is being asked for.

name.description: What it is called, as the catalogue titles it rather than as the agent named it.

why.description: The agent's case for connecting it, and the only words on this card that are the agent's.

amountUsd.description: The exact price. Not a ceiling: this scheme has no ranges, so this is the whole spend.

assetName.description: That token's name. It is pegged to the dollar, which is what lets every amount here read as dollars.

dailyCapUsd.description: What may go out in a day.

description.description: What the endpoint says it is.

spentTodayUsd.description: What has already gone out today.

url.description: What is being paid for.

approve.description: Whether to go ahead. Approving means the plan then runs without asking again per tool, because being asked whether a plan you just approved may run its first command is not a question worth having.

feedback.description: Why not, which goes back to the model as the reason.

requestId.description: Which card you are answering, from the frame that raised it.

answers.description: What you chose, keyed by the question, with the chosen labels or your own words.

cancelled.description: Dismissing it instead, which tells the agent to carry on using sensible defaults rather than leaving it waiting.

decision.description: Once allows this call alone; always allows that whole tool for the rest of the conversation; no blocks it.

helped.description: Whether you cleared it. Yes means the turn carries on from the page as you left it; no tells the agent so, and it moves on rather than waiting for ever.

kind.description: Answering a request for help in the agent's browser: a captcha, a password it does not hold, a check on your phone.

note.description: Anything the agent should know, which goes back to it either way.

helped.description: Whether you did it. Yes also hands the agent what the terminal now says, because a person answering a prompt is exactly the moment the agent cannot see.

kind.description: Answering a request for help at a terminal: a code to type, a confirmation only a person can give.

note.description: Anything the agent should know, which goes back to it either way.

approve.description: Yes releases exactly one run. Anything else charges nothing. This click is the only way the spend can happen.

kind.description: Answering a request to spend on a paid service.

connect.description: Yes keeps the agent waiting while you set it up, and it carries on the moment the connection comes alive. No tells it to continue without. The reply itself connects nothing: setting it up is still your own doing.

kind.description: Answering a request to connect something the agent needs.

approve.description: Yes releases exactly one payment. Anything else spends nothing. This click is the only way the money can move.

kind.description: The run is over and every frame has been delivered. A stream that closes without this was dropped mid-run, so re-attach with the last position you hold rather than assuming the turn finished.

after.description: The last frame you already have. Everything after it replays, then the stream goes live. Leave it out to start from the beginning.

run.description: The run you were watching. If a newer turn has started since, the stream replays that one from its beginning instead.

authorizeUrl.description: Where to send somebody to sign in.

state.description: The handshake's own id, sent back with it.

verifier.description: Keep this and send it back when finishing. It is what proves the code that comes back belongs to this handshake.

art.description: This extension's own mark, as a complete SVG document inline: the tier an author controls fully. category.description: Which section of the Extensions tab this sits under: a grouping by what it is FOR, which cannot be derived from what it contributes. A section this app has never heard of lands in 'Other' rather than failing to install.

agent.description: Declare that this checkout is also a Claude Code plugin, so the agent picks up its skills, agents, hooks, commands and MCP servers each turn. The daemon hands the directory to the plugin loader and never parses what is in it.

path.description: Relative to the extension checkout. Absent ⇒ the checkout root.

automationTemplates.description: Starting points this pack offers in the automation composer, a trigger, a prompt written for that trigger's payload, and whatever guard makes it safe to leave on. chore.description: Whether what this makes watches THIS codebase rather than the outside world. Declared rather than read off the trigger: a nightly dependency sweep and a nightly Stripe poll are both schedules.

guard.description: A condition that must hold before the turn runs: what makes a template safe to leave switched on.

holdForSeconds.description: Wait this long and coalesce repeats, rather than firing on every event.

icon.description: A name from the host's icon set, drawn when no simple-icons slug fits.

id.description: Prefills the automation name, and is what "does one of these exist already" is asked by, so spell it as an id, not as prose.

logo.description: A simple-icons slug for the card.

offer.description: Absent ⇒ it waits in the gallery, where you go once you know what you want. `create` puts a card on the page that makes it, switched off, in one click. `configure` puts one there that opens the dialog prefilled, for a template that cannot work unconfigured. prompt.description: The turn this starts. You own the trigger's payload vocabulary, so you own the prompt that reads it.

requires.description: Capability providers that make this template work: any one connected is enough (fixing CI rides github or gitlab). Omitted ⇒ nothing to connect, so it is always offered.

setup.description: What the user must do themselves before this can work.

trigger.description: What wakes it. Checked against the real trigger schema when the daemon builds the catalogue, so a template can never offer one that would be refused.

bin.description: A checkout-relative directory of executables the daemon puts on the agent's PATH every turn, how you ship the agent a command-line tool. The files are the approved code themselves: they ride the pinned checkout, and the daemon only adds the directory to PATH.

capabilities.description: Capability cards this pack adds to the "+" grid: a connected CLI tool, a site the agent acts on as the owner through the shared browser, an operating system pack, or a preset over a core kind. guide.description: The walkthrough the install dialog renders for getting the credential this card asks for.

icon.description: A name from the host's own icon set, drawn when no simple-icons slug fits. It ships in the image, follows the theme and costs no request: what actually carries a first-party extension. An unknown name falls back to initials rather than to a hole.

env.description: The environment the agent's shell gets, as value templates over the fields: `${field}` substitutes, `${field:uri}` percent-encodes. Each name is suffixed per instance.

boolean.description: Render it as a switch, carrying "on"/"off". For an opt-in EXTRA rather than a decision: a two-option picker says the same thing but presents a choice the user must make to proceed, sized like the required fields around it. A switch always holds a value, so a field like this never blocks a submit.

hint.description: A line under this control, for what the label alone cannot say: a host requirement, when a value takes effect. The card's own `hint` speaks for the whole card; this one is bound to the field it qualifies.

options.description: Turns the field into a select.

rebuild.description: This value only takes effect after the sandbox is rebuilt, because it rides the image overlay. Shown as a chip beside the label: two switches side by side, identical in every visible way, can otherwise cost five seconds or five minutes with no way to tell which.

secret.description: Mask it, and never echo it back.

totp.description: This field holds a TOTP seed, the base32 key or otpauth:// URI a service shows when enrolling an authenticator app. Declare it with `secret: true`. Unlike an ordinary secret it never enters the agent's environment: the daemon mints the six-digit codes on demand and only those cross.

value.description: A fixed value baked into the config rather than asked for: how a card pins its discriminator (platform="reddit", provider="stripe"). Renders as nothing.

when.description: Only show this field while a condition over the answers already given holds: `auth == 'key'`, `provider in ['ipsec', 'fortinet']`, `!advanced`. Supports `&&`, `||`, `!`, comparisons and `in`.

fragment.description: A Dockerfile fragment holding the client binary this tool needs (psql, mysql, whisper).

pack.description: A sandbox feature pack name (whisper, llamacpp, browser, …) supplying this tool. Preferred over `fragment`: an image that already bakes the pack needs no rebuild, and there is no copy to drift.

skill.description: Checkout-relative SKILL.md teaching the agent this tool. `${id}` in it is replaced with the instance name at apply time.

commands.description: Commands this extension may register handlers for, surfaced in the command palette. Title, icon and shortcut all come from here rather than from the registration call, because this is what the owner approved at install.

icon.description: A name from the host's icon set, drawn beside the title.

keybinding.description: A global keyboard shortcut, e.g. "Mod+Shift+K" — `Mod` is ⌘ on Apple and Ctrl elsewhere. Declared here because a global shortcut is consequential: the owner approves it at install, and the host binds only what was approved.

title.description: What the command palette shows. The manifest's value wins over the one passed at registration.

when.description: When the shortcut applies, as a condition over the shell's context keys, `tabSurface == 'chat'`, `!editableTarget`. Without one the chord is claimed everywhere, including inside a terminal where a bare key belongs to the program running in it. The command palette ignores this: a command is always runnable by name.

documents.description: Per-directory documents this extension can offer. Your provider marks the rows in the Workspace tree it has something to say about, and the host opens your component as a tab.

label.description: The family's name, shown in the install dialog beside your other contributions. Per-row wording stays with the provider, which is the only thing that knows what it found.

environment.description: A Dockerfile fragment baked into the sandbox image so your tools are actually installed at runtime: a whisper binary, a psql client. The owner approves the composed overlay and rebuilds out of band, so this does not take effect immediately.

fragment.description: Checkout-relative path to a file holding ONLY RUN and ENV instructions. FROM and privileged directives are rejected: those stay daemon-owned.

files.description: Which workspace files back your views, so the daemon's file watcher can tell the browser they went stale instead of you polling for it. The agent edits the workspace out of band from every HTTP route, and this push is the only thing that can notice.

invalidates.description: The query keys this path makes stale, the first element of your own api.sandbox.key(...) keys. Keep both this and the path as narrow as the view actually needs: a broad prefix costs every connected browser a refetch on every matching write.

path.description: Workspace-root-relative, forward-slash, matched by prefix, so one entry covers an exact file (`.intentic/config/automations.json`), a directory (`.intentic/config/drafts/`, with the trailing slash so it cannot match a sibling file) or a name family (`.intentic/environment.`). Not a glob.

listener.description: A realtime event source this extension supplies, so automations can trigger on it. One declaration feeds both halves: the daemon accepts these event types and serves this provider's control surface, and the automation editor derives its source picker, filters and starter prompt from it, so a newly installed listener is configurable without a matching app release.

automation.description: How the generic automation editor presents this source: its name, its filters, and the prompt it starts people on.

branchField.description: A second narrowing axis, for a source whose events carry one: a pipeline's git ref, so a trigger can say "the branch that ships" rather than "every agent's every failure".

hint.description: The sentence under the input, for a filter whose empty case is easy to get wrong.

channel.description: The primary narrowing filter, a channel, a room, a repo.

hint.description: The sentence under the input, for a filter whose empty case is easy to get wrong.

mentionLabel.description: Only for a source whose message events distinguish being addressed. Absent ⇒ the editor offers no mention-only filter, rather than inventing semantics you did not promise.

starterPrompt.description: The first prompt a new automation on this source is prefilled with. You own the payload vocabulary, so you own the prompt that explains it.

events.description: The event types this source can fire, with the wording the automation editor offers them under. The daemon accepts no others.

provider.description: The slug this source's automation triggers fire on.

processes.description: Long-lived background processes the daemon runs for this extension: a gateway holding a connection the daemon must not, a dev server. Managed the same way panel dev servers are, and startable and stoppable from the Extensions tab.

autoStart.description: Launch it on install and on daemon boot, rather than waiting to be started.

cwd.description: Relative to the extension checkout. Absent ⇒ the checkout root.

port.description: Assign a free port and inject it as PORT.

preview.description: Expose the port on a tunnelled preview hostname.

settings.description: Typed settings the host renders into the Settings page for you and persists daemon-side. You never draw the form or store the value; you read it back with api.settings.get.

description.description: The line under the control.

enum.description: The choices, for type "enum". Meaningless otherwise.

env.description: Inject the stored value into the agent's shell environment under this name, every turn. How a credential you hold reaches the agent's command-line tools.

secret.description: Mask the value in the UI and strip it from reads: a set secret round-trips as 'still set', never as its value.

type.description: Which control the Settings page draws. `enum` reads its choices from `enum`.

viewers.description: File formats this extension can render. The host resolves an opened file to your viewer by its extension, fetches the content, and renders your component with it: you keep none of the fetch lifecycle and none of the daemon credentials.

extensions.description: Bare file extensions, no dot: e.g. ["docx", "xlsx"].

fetch.description: How much of the file the host hands you. `text` for a format that is text (svg, a subtitle track). `blob` for one that must be parsed end to end before any of it shows (a .docx, a spreadsheet), bounded by the daemon's raw-read cap. `url` for anything range-read rather than parsed (audio, video): your component gets a streaming URL to point an element at, never the bytes.

views.description: Sidebar elements this extension may register at runtime. Each entry reserves an id and a surface; the extension supplies the component with api.views.register, and the host refuses any registration this list does not cover.

badge.description: Allow this view to put a count on its tile. Declared because a badge interrupts from every other screen in the app; leave it out and any badge the extension registers is dropped.

label.description: The name shown on the tile or tab. The manifest's value wins over the one passed at registration.

surface.description: Where it appears. `rail` is a tile in the global left rail; `directory` is a panel opened from a repo in the Workspace tree; `sandbox` is a tab on the Sandbox hub, for a view whose subject is the box rather than the work.

engines.description: A semver range over the host's extension API version, checked before your code is activated.

entry.description: Repo-relative path of your prebuilt single-file ESM bundle, built with `vue` and `@intentic/extension-api` as externals. Absent ⇒ an extension with no UI.

icon.description: A name from the host's own icon set, drawn when no simple-icons slug fits. It ships in the image, follows the theme and costs no request: what actually carries a first-party extension. An unknown name falls back to initials rather than to a hole.

logo.description: A simple-icons slug, fetched from a CDN: right for standing in for somebody else's product. Add a "/<hex>" suffix to force a colour for a mark that vanishes against the surface it lands on. Unreachable in an offline sandbox, so it falls back to `icon`, then to initials.

permissions.description: How far this extension may reach into the daemon, as "<METHOD> <path-glob>" entries where `*` matches one path segment: e.g. "GET /panels", "POST /panels/*/start". The install dialog shows these, the host refuses anything undeclared, and the usage ledger records which were actually earned.

sandbox.description: Daemon routes your UI half may call. Your own backend namespace needs no entry: its backend is your own code.

server.description: Repo-relative path of your prebuilt single-file node ESM server bundle, exporting `activateServer`. Served under your own route namespace, which the daemon proxies. Nothing is provided at runtime but node builtins, so bundle everything else in. Absent ⇒ no backend.

previous.description: The version kept one step back, which is what going back means.

ref.description: The commit that was running before.

rebuildNeeded.description: The new version changes what the sandbox image contains, so a one-time rebuild is still pending and the update is not wholly landed yet.

advisories.description: What to do about a security warning: switch it off at once, or tell you.

updates.description: What to do about a newer version: tell you, have an agent read the difference first, or just take it.

compatible.description: Whether this sandbox is one of them.

engines.description: Which sandbox versions the new one says it needs.

powers.description: Exactly what the new code asks for that the running one does not. This is what approving an update is approving.

added.description: What the new version asks for that the running one does not. The whole point of the comparison.

removed.description: What it no longer asks for.

url.description: Where it comes from.

checkedAt.description: When, so a screen can date the answer.

used.description: Which of its declared powers it exercised, and how many times.

advisory.description: A security warning about the installed version.

autoDisabled.description: Whether the sandbox has already switched it off.

reason.description: Why the registry pulled the listing, in its own words. Delisting protects people browsing; this record is for the person already running it.

backend.description: Present only for an extension that ships a server half.

detail.description: What went wrong, so a backend that failed to start is a sentence rather than an address that answers nothing.

state.description: How its server half is doing. Absent means the code is not in this image at all; incompatible means it needs a different sandbox version.

enabled.description: The owner's switch. A switched-off extension is still listed, which is what makes it switchable back on, but nothing it contributes is wired up.

essential.description: Its switch is fixed on, because it is the only way to see or stop an engine the sandbox runs regardless. health.description: How it has behaved since the last update, which is what decides whether that update sticks.

autoReverted.description: The update was already rolled back without anybody asking. The record stays rather than pretending the attempt never happened.

detail.description: What is going wrong, when something is.

fromRef.description: Which version it was updated from, which is what going back would return to.

state.description: How it has behaved since the last update. Checks catch broken, not wrong, so for a while after a swap it is simply watched.

manifest.description: What it declares about itself: what it contributes, what it needs, and what it may reach.

$schema.description: The authoring schema, for editor completion and validation. Nothing at runtime reads it.

art.description: This extension's own mark, as a complete SVG document inline: the tier an author controls fully. Give it a viewBox and let it fill its own square edge to edge; it is drawn as the tile, not as a glyph on a plate. category.description: Which section of the Extensions tab this sits under: a grouping by what it is FOR, which cannot be derived from what it contributes. A section this app has never heard of lands in 'Other' rather than failing to install.

agent.description: Declare that this checkout is also a Claude Code plugin, so the agent picks up its skills, agents, hooks, commands and MCP servers each turn. The daemon hands the directory to the plugin loader and never parses what is in it.

path.description: Relative to the extension checkout. Absent ⇒ the checkout root.

automationTemplates.description: Starting points this pack offers in the automation composer, a trigger, a prompt written for that trigger's payload, and whatever guard makes it safe to leave on. chore.description: Whether what this makes watches THIS codebase rather than the outside world. Declared rather than read off the trigger: a nightly dependency sweep and a nightly Stripe poll are both schedules.

guard.description: A condition that must hold before the turn runs: what makes a template safe to leave switched on.

holdForSeconds.description: Wait this long and coalesce repeats, rather than firing on every event.

icon.description: A name from the host's icon set, drawn when no simple-icons slug fits.

id.description: Prefills the automation name, and is what "does one of these exist already" is asked by, so spell it as an id, not as prose.

logo.description: A simple-icons slug for the card.

offer.description: Absent ⇒ it waits in the gallery, where you go once you know what you want. `create` puts a card on the page that makes it, switched off, in one click. `configure` puts one there that opens the dialog prefilled, for a template that cannot work unconfigured. prompt.description: The turn this starts. You own the trigger's payload vocabulary, so you own the prompt that reads it.

requires.description: Capability providers that make this template work: any one connected is enough (fixing CI rides github or gitlab). Omitted ⇒ nothing to connect, so it is always offered.

setup.description: What the user must do themselves before this can work.

trigger.description: What wakes it. Checked against the real trigger schema when the daemon builds the catalogue, so a template can never offer one that would be refused.

bin.description: A checkout-relative directory of executables the daemon puts on the agent's PATH every turn, how you ship the agent a command-line tool. The files are the approved code themselves: they ride the pinned checkout, and the daemon only adds the directory to PATH.

capabilities.description: Capability cards this pack adds to the "+" grid: a connected CLI tool, a site the agent acts on as the owner through the shared browser, an operating system pack, or a preset over a core kind. boolean.description: Render it as a switch, carrying "on"/"off". fragment.description: A Dockerfile fragment holding the client binary this tool needs (psql, mysql, whisper).

pack.description: A sandbox feature pack name (whisper, llamacpp, browser, …) supplying this tool. Preferred over `fragment`: an image that already bakes the pack needs no rebuild, and there is no copy to drift.

skill.description: Checkout-relative SKILL.md teaching the agent this tool. `${id}` in it is replaced with the instance name at apply time.

commands.description: Commands this extension may register handlers for, surfaced in the command palette. Title, icon and shortcut all come from here rather than from the registration call, because this is what the owner approved at install.

icon.description: A name from the host's icon set, drawn beside the title.

keybinding.description: A global keyboard shortcut, e.g. "Mod+Shift+K" — `Mod` is ⌘ on Apple and Ctrl elsewhere. Declared here because a global shortcut is consequential: the owner approves it at install, and the host binds only what was approved.

title.description: What the command palette shows. The manifest's value wins over the one passed at registration.

when.description: When the shortcut applies, as a condition over the shell's context keys, `tabSurface == 'chat'`, `!editableTarget`. Without one the chord is claimed everywhere, including inside a terminal where a bare key belongs to the program running in it. The command palette ignores this: a command is always runnable by name.

documents.description: Per-directory documents this extension can offer. Your provider marks the rows in the Workspace tree it has something to say about, and the host opens your component as a tab.

label.description: The family's name, shown in the install dialog beside your other contributions. Per-row wording stays with the provider, which is the only thing that knows what it found.

environment.description: A Dockerfile fragment baked into the sandbox image so your tools are actually installed at runtime: a whisper binary, a psql client. The owner approves the composed overlay and rebuilds out of band, so this does not take effect immediately.

fragment.description: Checkout-relative path to a file holding ONLY RUN and ENV instructions. FROM and privileged directives are rejected: those stay daemon-owned.

files.description: Which workspace files back your views, so the daemon's file watcher can tell the browser they went stale instead of you polling for it. The agent edits the workspace out of band from every HTTP route, and this push is the only thing that can notice.

invalidates.description: The query keys this path makes stale, the first element of your own api.sandbox.key(...) keys. Keep both this and the path as narrow as the view actually needs: a broad prefix costs every connected browser a refetch on every matching write.

path.description: Workspace-root-relative, forward-slash, matched by prefix, so one entry covers an exact file (`.intentic/config/automations.json`), a directory (`.intentic/config/drafts/`, with the trailing slash so it cannot match a sibling file) or a name family (`.intentic/environment.`). Not a glob.

listener.description: A realtime event source this extension supplies, so automations can trigger on it. One declaration feeds both halves: the daemon accepts these event types and serves this provider's control surface, and the automation editor derives its source picker, filters and starter prompt from it, so a newly installed listener is configurable without a matching app release.

automation.description: How the generic automation editor presents this source: its name, its filters, and the prompt it starts people on.

branchField.description: A second narrowing axis, for a source whose events carry one: a pipeline's git ref, so a trigger can say "the branch that ships" rather than "every agent's every failure".

hint.description: The sentence under the input, for a filter whose empty case is easy to get wrong.

channel.description: The primary narrowing filter, a channel, a room, a repo.

mentionLabel.description: Only for a source whose message events distinguish being addressed. Absent ⇒ the editor offers no mention-only filter, rather than inventing semantics you did not promise.

starterPrompt.description: The first prompt a new automation on this source is prefilled with. You own the payload vocabulary, so you own the prompt that explains it.

events.description: The event types this source can fire, with the wording the automation editor offers them under. The daemon accepts no others.

provider.description: The slug this source's automation triggers fire on.

processes.description: Long-lived background processes the daemon runs for this extension: a gateway holding a connection the daemon must not, a dev server. Managed the same way panel dev servers are, and startable and stoppable from the Extensions tab.

autoStart.description: Launch it on install and on daemon boot, rather than waiting to be started.

cwd.description: Relative to the extension checkout. Absent ⇒ the checkout root.

port.description: Assign a free port and inject it as PORT.

preview.description: Expose the port on a tunnelled preview hostname.

settings.description: Typed settings the host renders into the Settings page for you and persists daemon-side. You never draw the form or store the value; you read it back with api.settings.get.

description.description: The line under the control.

enum.description: The choices, for type "enum". Meaningless otherwise.

env.description: Inject the stored value into the agent's shell environment under this name, every turn. How a credential you hold reaches the agent's command-line tools.

secret.description: Mask the value in the UI and strip it from reads: a set secret round-trips as 'still set', never as its value.

type.description: Which control the Settings page draws. `enum` reads its choices from `enum`.

viewers.description: File formats this extension can render. The host resolves an opened file to your viewer by its extension, fetches the content, and renders your component with it: you keep none of the fetch lifecycle and none of the daemon credentials.

extensions.description: Bare file extensions, no dot: e.g. ["docx", "xlsx"].

fetch.description: How much of the file the host hands you. `text` for a format that is text (svg, a subtitle track). `blob` for one that must be parsed end to end before any of it shows (a .docx, a spreadsheet), bounded by the daemon's raw-read cap. `url` for anything range-read rather than parsed (audio, video): your component gets a streaming URL to point an element at, never the bytes.

views.description: Sidebar elements this extension may register at runtime. Each entry reserves an id and a surface; the extension supplies the component with api.views.register, and the host refuses any registration this list does not cover.

badge.description: Allow this view to put a count on its tile. Declared because a badge interrupts from every other screen in the app; leave it out and any badge the extension registers is dropped.

label.description: The name shown on the tile or tab. The manifest's value wins over the one passed at registration.

surface.description: Where it appears. `rail` is a tile in the global left rail; `directory` is a panel opened from a repo in the Workspace tree; `sandbox` is a tab on the Sandbox hub, for a view whose subject is the box rather than the work.

engines.description: A semver range over the host's extension API version, checked before your code is activated.

entry.description: Repo-relative path of your prebuilt single-file ESM bundle, built with `vue` and `@intentic/extension-api` as externals. Absent ⇒ an extension with no UI.

autoTier.description: Whether an easy-looking turn may run on a cheaper model from the same provider. Three states rather than a switch, because the middle one is the only honest road to the third: it scores every turn and routes nothing, so the guess can become a measurement before it changes anything. autoTierEagerness.description: How readily a turn counts as simple enough for the cheaper model. It moves only the cutoff: at every setting a turn still has to say something positively easy, so nothing here can downgrade a short vague request.

automationFailureLimit.description: How many failures in a row before an automation switches itself off. commandRules.description: What an agent may run inside the sandbox, for the five kinds of command that are hard to take back: rewriting git history, deleting recursively, reading credential files, publishing a package, reaching out to the network. hashlineEdits.description: Have the agent edit files by line number rather than by quoting the text it wants replaced. Cheaper on large files, and less forgiving of a stale read.

iqSearch.description: Teach the agent how to use this workspace's own search tool, rather than leaving it to grep around.

iqSearchHoldout.description: What share of conversations to run without that teaching, so the two can be compared. Whole conversations rather than individual turns, because once the teaching is in a session, withholding it from the next request does not make the model forget it.

outputHoldout.description: What share of commands to leave untrimmed, so the saving can be measured against a real comparison rather than estimated.

quickModel.description: Which models do the small automatic jobs that are not a conversation, such as writing a commit message. resumeAfterOutage.description: Whether a turn killed by the model provider failing is re-run automatically, backing off between attempts.
